title: 第1624章 剑流看世第1623章 贵族质疑
content_zh:
周遭贵族纷纷附和，压抑多日的恐慌与愤懑尽数宣泄而出。
有人沉声怒斥：“没有世家镇抚地方、供给赋税、戍守边疆，索西亚拿什么立国？靠那些目不识丁、只会跟风作乱的泥腿子？”
还有人语气绝望又怨毒：“他清空王庭、颠覆乡序，杀光有功绩、有底蕴的旧族。”
“最后...！只会落得朝野无人、天下大乱！老夫看他不是换血，是要让整个王国流血流干！”
众说纷纭，句句都是根深蒂固的傲慢与不解。
在他们的认知里，世家就是索西亚的骨血，是江山存续的根本，剔除世家，便是断绝国运，除此之外再无第二种可能。
可。
这是真的。
试想一下。
在你的认知里，意气用事，可以一次性杀光所有贪官。
可杀完之后呢？
他们的位置谁来胜任？
有些东西，需要很高的专业性，需要很强的人际关系，会牵扯到很多企业、产业，但一个产权变更，下面都会争的头破血流。
而且人性本就贪婪。
你一个一个杀，也根本解决不掉。
因为，贪官诞生的速度，和你杀掉的速度，极有可能不匹配。
杀慢了，没效果，还招人记恨。
杀快了，岗位失调，制度压力飙升。
这，的确是有道理。
他们也并非完全的“无脑傲慢”，而是有着自己理解的“傲慢”。

普罗旺斯静静听着众人的斥责与争辩，面色毫无波澜，没有辩解，也没有动怒。
他只是微微垂眸，视线落在自己布满老茧、宽厚有力的手掌上。
这双手曾握重甲长剑，驰骋沙场破敌无数，也曾执教习长剑，数十年如一日打磨武道、传授技艺。
比起朝堂上虚无缥缈的权术博弈，他一辈子信奉的，从来都是最直白、最残酷的强弱逻辑。
待到众人声浪稍稍平息，满室目光再度死死锁在他身上，等待他的荒唐说辞不攻自破时，老者才再度开口，声音不高，却带着穿透一切嘈杂的力量。
“你们只看见了世家要死，却没看见，他在往这具早已腐朽的躯体里，灌新血。”
他抬眼，目光锐利如出鞘剑锋，扫过满屋锦衣贵族。
“你们以为，王权忌惮的是我们的兵权、我们的田产？错了。王权真正忌惮的，是壁垒。”
“文武分流，贵贱有别，富者代代习武掌权，贫者世世耕田为奴。主流三派剑术，秋水流、孤山流、破居流，堂堂国之武道，立国之战技，千百年来，从未真正走出过贵族庄园。”
普罗旺斯的语气带着一丝唏嘘，更多的是冰冷的通透。
“你们都说穷文富武，以此为尊，以此为贵。”
“你们靠着资源垄断武道，靠着武道稳固特权，靠着特权世代欺压乡土。”
content_en:
The surrounding nobles all echoed, and all the panic and anger that had been suppressed for many days was vented.
Someone shouted angrily: "Without aristocratic families to control the local area, provide taxes, and guard the borders, how can Sosia build a country? Rely on those ignorant people who only follow the trend and cause chaos?"
Others sounded desperate and resentful: "He emptied the royal court, overturned the order of the village, and killed all the old clans with meritorious deeds and heritage."
"In the end...! It will only end up with no one in the government and the public, and the world will be in chaos! I think he is not changing blood, but letting the entire kingdom bleed dry!"
There are different opinions, and every one of them is full of deep-rooted arrogance and incomprehension.
In their understanding, the aristocratic family is the flesh and blood of Sosia and the foundation for the survival of the country. Eliminating the aristocratic family means cutting off the destiny of the country. There is no other possibility.
Can.
It's true.
Just think about it.
In your opinion, you can kill all corrupt officials at once by acting on your own initiative.
But what happens after the killing?
Who will fill their position?
Some things require a high degree of professionalism and strong interpersonal relationships, and will involve many companies and industries, but a change in property rights will cause a bloody battle among the following.
And human nature is inherently greedy.
Even if you kill them one by one, you won't be able to solve them at all.
Because the speed at which corrupt officials are born and the speed at which you kill them are very likely not to match.
Killing is slow, ineffective, and makes people hate you.
Killings are quick, positions are out of balance, and pressure on the system is soaring.
This does make sense.
They are not completely "brainless arrogance", but have their own understanding of "arrogance".
Provence listened quietly to everyone's reprimands and arguments, his expression unmoved, neither defensive nor angry.
He just lowered his eyes slightly, his eyes falling on his calloused, broad and strong palms.
These hands once held heavy armor and long swords, and galloped on the battlefield to defeat countless enemies. They also taught long swordsmen, honing martial arts and teaching skills for decades.
Compared with the illusory power games in the court, what he believed in all his life was the most straightforward and cruel logic of strength and weakness.
When the crowd's noise subsided a little, and the eyes of the whole room were locked on him again, waiting for his absurd remarks to be self-defeating, the old man spoke again, his voice was not high, but it had the power to penetrate all the noise.
"You only saw that the noble family was dying, but you didn't see that he was pouring new blood into this already rotten body."
He raised his eyes, his eyes as sharp as an unsheathed sword, sweeping across the room full of nobles in rich robes.
"You think that what the royal power is afraid of is our military power and our land? You are wrong. What the royal power is really afraid of is barriers."
"Civil and martial arts are separated, and there is a distinction between high and low. The rich have practiced martial arts for generations and have been in power, while the poor have been working as slaves for generations. The three main schools of swordsmanship, Qiushui Liuliu, Gushanliu, and Pojuliu, the martial arts of a dignified country and the combat skills of establishing a country, have never truly left the noble manor for thousands of years."
Provence's tone was a bit sad, but more of a cold and transparent one.
"You all say that the poor in literature and the rich in martial arts are respected and honored by this."
"You rely on resources to monopolize martial arts, rely on martial arts to consolidate your privileges, and rely on privileges to oppress the countryside for generations."
